description: Grounding map: every quantitative paper claim traced to artifact.

claims.claim: 100% phase classification accuracy on 72 configurations (4 activations × 3 depths × 6 σ_w values)
claims.verification: 72 configs, 2 seeds per config, majority vote. Validated against actual MNIST training outcomes.

claims.claim: Depth-calibrated per-layer chi thresholds [10^(-4/L), 10^(4/L)] match training outcomes
claims.verification: Calibrated against 72 real training experiments. Theory: per-layer chi must be closer to 1.0 for deeper networks.

claims.claim: SUPERSEDED by CaliKit: Calibrated PhaseKit wins 10/31 configs (best of 7 methods, avg rank 3.52). Previous PhaseKit theory-only won 7/10 on narrow comparison, then 3/15 on broader comparison.
claims.verification: 32 configs, 2 seeds each. SGD regression, 300 steps. 7 methods compared.
claims.ng_superseded: CaliKit + GS-CaliKit combined: 24/32 wins (75%) with zero divergence (see ng-init-comparison-75pct)

claims.claim: κ₄ excess kurtosis growth exponent = 0.109 (sub-linear in depth). 95th percentile |κ₄| = 14.76.
claims.verification: 50 networks per config, widths 64-1024, 4 activations, 20 layers.

claims.claim: At criticality, κ₄ accumulation has growth exponent 0.109. For depth 50: max|κ₄| = 2.35.
claims.verification: 100 trials per depth, ReLU, width=256, depths 5-50.
MLPs, CNNs, ResNets, VGG, MobileNet, DenseNet, Transformers.

claims.claim: 95.1% phase classification on 61 architectures across 19 families
Stochastic crossover width scales as Δ ~ N^{-0.5}, R² > 0.99 for all activations
claims.verification: Monte Carlo with widths 64-2048, 10000 networks per point.

claims.claim: O(1/N²) corrections give 3.4× improvement in variance prediction at width 32
20 Z3-verified properties (algebraic identities P1-P7, convergence P8-P12, finite-width P13-P20)
claims.verification: All properties return unsat in <1s. These are algebraic sanity checks, not system-level guarantees.

claims.claim: q^{l+1} = σ_w² V(q^l) + σ_b² with V(q) = E[φ(√q·z)²]
claims.verification: Poole et al. (2016), Schoenholz et al. (2017). Validated empirically across 9 activations.

claims.claim: Init-time critical σ_w differs from fixed-point σ_w* for non-ReLU activations
claims.verification: For GELU: σ_w*(fp)=1.982, σ_w*(init)=1.481. Validated by training experiments.

claims.claim: PhaseKit-NG achieves 96.4% phase classification accuracy on 336 configurations (4 activations × 4 depths × 3 widths × 7 σ_w values)
claims.details: Standard PhaseKit: 51.8% on same configs. NG improvement: +44.6%. ReLU 100%, GELU 100%, SiLU 92.9%, tanh 92.9%. Depth 10: 96.4% (was 55%).
claims.methodology: Ground truth from MC forward passes (20 trials), classified by geometric mean variance ratio. NG classifier uses coupled (variance, kurtosis) recursion + MC calibration.

claims.claim: CaliKit + GS-CaliKit win 24/32 init configs combined (75%), with zero inf-loss failures
claims.details: CaliKit: 13/32 wins (41%), GS-CaliKit: 11/32 wins (34%). Xavier: 2/32, Kaiming: 0/32, LSUV: 3/32, PhaseKit: 3/32. Zero inf-loss failures for both CaliKit variants.
claims.methodology: Full-network SGD training for 200 steps with gradient clipping, 4 depths × 2 widths × 4 activations.

claims.claim: Coupled (variance, kurtosis) recursion tracks non-Gaussian effects through depth with activation-adaptive corrections
claims.details: Recursion: q^(l+1) = σ_w² V(q^(l)) + σ_b², κ^(l+1) = κ_act(q^(l)) + κ^(l) · χ_1² / N. Effective chi: χ_eff = σ_w² · χ_1 · (1 + κ · σ_w² / (2N)).
claims.methodology: Novel theoretical contribution extending standard mean-field theory.

claims.claim: GS-CaliKit initialization has zero inf-loss failures across all tested configurations including depth 20
claims.details: Standard CaliKit had inf losses at depth 10-20 for ReLU/GELU/SiLU. GS-CaliKit uses empirical σ_w search with stability verification to prevent divergence.
claims.methodology: 32 configurations: 4 depths × 2 widths × 4 activations, 200-step SGD training.
